Checked rule adoption, publication, county clerk filing, facility copies on file, and permissive temporary or permanent privilege suspension for persons or corporations. Revised subsection 1 title to remove "posting" in favor of "filing" to match the source requirement to keep copies on file; retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Adoption, publication, and filing of library use rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 681). Directs the urban district board to adopt reasonable rules governing library use and privileges, publish them with amendments, file them with the served county clerk, and keep copies on file in all public library facilities. Independent review removed "posting" because the source requires keeping copies on file in library facilities.

headings.title: Temporary or permanent suspension of library privileges for rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants permissive authority to the board or librarian to suspend a violating person's or corporation's library privileges temporarily or permanently as deemed in the best interests of the urban library and people served.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 681) and verified all fingerprints. Verified school-district library property transfer under sections 182.701–182.723, former nonlibrary property with library building and postal facility, dual-purpose property retention with non-mandatory lease agreement, and transfer of library-only reversionary/leasehold rights and rental obligations (retaining source phrase "except as otherwise provided for this section"). Revised subsection 4 title to include transferred obligations alongside rights; retained subsections 1–3.

headings.title: Transfer of school district real property used for public libraries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 681). Subject to subsections 2 and 3, transfers all right, title, and interest of a nine-director urban school district in real property and improvements used or acquired for public library purposes to the coterminous urban public library district upon creation under sections 182.701 to 182.723.

headings.title: Transfer of former nonlibrary property with library and postal facility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Transfers to the new urban public library district any school-district real property formerly used for nonlibrary purposes that at election time had a public library building containing a postal facility.

headings.title: Retention of dual-purpose property and optional lease agreement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Retains in the nine-director urban school district any real property or improvements funded or dedicated for both library and nonlibrary purposes; requires agreed rental payments under a duly executed lease if the library occupies space, without obligating the school district to permit use.

headings.title: Transfer of reversionary, leasehold, and library-only rights and obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Transfers to the new urban public library district all reversionary, leasehold, and other real property rights and obligations (including rental obligations) pertaining solely to public library property, subject to section exceptions (retaining source phrase "except as otherwise provided for this section"). Independent review revised title to include transferred real property obligations alongside rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections including subsection 1 subdivisions (1)–(2) and paragraphs (a)–(i), subsection 2 YES/NO ballot table and continuation paragraph, and history notes (L. 2011 H.B. 161 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1561) and verified all fingerprints. Checked sections 144.010–144.525 and 32.085/32.087 cross-references, retained source quirks ("under this subsection" in subsection 2 and "if no individuals are eligible and registered to vote reside" in subsection 3), and verified definitions. Revised subsection 1 title to remove "half-cent" so the up-to-one-half-cent ceiling is not misstated as a fixed rate; retained subsections 2–4.

headings.title: Eligible counties and voter-approved library sales tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), paragraphs (a) through (i), and history notes (L. 2011 H.B. 161 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1561). Lists nine population/classification county categories and authorizes listed public library districts, by board majority vote and voter approval at a county or state general, primary, or special election, to impose an additional retail sales tax up to one-half cent under sections 144.010 to 144.525 for library operation and maintenance. Independent review removed "half-cent" from title to avoid suggesting a fixed rate where the statute sets a ceiling up to one-half cent.

headings.title: Sales tax ballot form, election outcome, and sections 32.085 and 32.087
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the YES/NO ballot table and continuation paragraph, and history notes. Sets out substantial sales-tax ballot language, specifies approval and rejection effects, and applies sections 32.085 and 32.087 to approved taxes. Independent review noted source text says "under this subsection" in both the opening clause and continuation paragraph referring to the tax authorized in subsection 1.

headings.title: Definition of qualified voters including property-owner consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Defines "qualified voters" or "voters" for section 182.802 as chapter 115 registered district residents, or unanimous consenting real property owners if no eligible registered voters reside in the proposed district (with governing bodies acting for political subdivision/corporate owners; retains source wording "if no individuals are eligible and registered to vote reside").

headings.title: Definition of public library district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Defines "public library district" for section 182.802 to include city, county, city-county, municipal, consolidated, and urban library districts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections including subsection 7 subdivisions (1)–(4) and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 300 § 1, A.L. 1995 S.B. 14) and verified all fingerprints. Verified library network definition, state librarian rulemaking and separate appropriations, nonreverting Library Networking Fund notwithstanding section 33.080, and neutral description of archived 1995 Joint Committee on Administrative Rules review/suspension/ratification and Article IV Section 8/section 536.037 revocation provisions without asserting current enforceability. Retained all 10 drafted titles as accurate and neutral.

headings.title: Definition of library network
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1983 H.B. 300 § 1, A.L. 1995 S.B. 14). Defines "library network" for section 182.812 as a formal process of cooperation between libraries and other entities to share and extend combined resources.

headings.title: State librarian rulemaking, separate appropriations, and network grants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the state librarian to promulgate rules administering general assembly library-network appropriations, keeps such appropriations separate from other state library appropriations, and governs grant certification and warrant issuance.

headings.title: Library Networking Fund establishment, nonreversion, and investment earnings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes the special Library Networking Fund in the state treasury for gifts, contributions, grants, and bequests, exempts fund moneys from general-revenue reversion notwithstanding section 33.080, and credits time-deposit yield, interest, and gains to the fund.

headings.title: Legislative rule review condition under joint committee on administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 1995 S.B. 14). Describes the archived statutory text conditioning effectiveness of section 182.812 rules on Joint Committee on Administrative Rules approval and legislative ratification procedures, without asserting current constitutional enforceability.

headings.title: Concurrent submission of proposed rules to joint committee and hearings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the state librarian to submit proposed rules to the Joint Committee on Administrative Rules concurrently with secretary of state filing and authorizes committee hearings at any time.

headings.title: Thirty-day committee review period before filing final rulemaking order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Bars filing a final order of rulemaking with the secretary of state until 30 days after committee receipt, permits hearings during that period, and deems the order approved if not disapproved within 30 days.

headings.title: Grounds for joint committee suspension of rulemaking order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note. Authorizes majority-vote committee suspension of a rulemaking order prior to filing only on four enumerated grounds: lack of statutory authority, public health/safety/welfare emergency, conflict with state law, or substantial change in circumstance.

headings.title: Bar on filing or publishing committee-disapproved rule portions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Prohibits the state librarian from filing and the secretary of state from publishing in the Missouri Register any portion of a final order of rulemaking disapproved by the committee.

headings.title: Committee report and legislative ratification of rule disapproval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs the committee to report disapproval findings to both houses and keeps disapproved rules from taking effect so long as both houses ratify the disapproval by resolution within 30 legislative days.

headings.title: Legislative suspension or revocation of adopted rules and register notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Describes archived text providing for suspension or revocation of adopted rules by bill or Article IV Section 8 concurrent resolution on committee recommendation, committee hearings under section 536.037, and Missouri Register notice publication.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections including subsection 1 subdivisions (1)–(2) and history note (L. 1986 H.B. 1372 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1085) and verified all fingerprints. Noted discrepancy between official catchline ("Disclosure of library records not required") and amended body text affirmatively prohibiting release/disclosure by libraries, staff, agents, and contracted third parties except upon written consent or public-safety/criminal-prosecution court order. Verified 180-day AG complaint, private civil action with asymmetric respondent fee standard, and permissive AG enforcement. Retained all 3 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosing library records and limited exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note (L. 1986 H.B. 1372 § 2, A.L. 2014 H.B. 1085). Notwithstanding contrary law, prohibits libraries, employees, agents, and contracted third parties from releasing or disclosing library records except upon written consent/request of the identified person per library procedures or a court order finding disclosure necessary to protect public safety or prosecute a crime. Independent review noted discrepancy between official catchline ("Disclosure of library records not required") and amended body text (affirmative prohibition on release or disclosure).

headings.title: Attorney general complaints, civil actions, damages, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits an affected person to file a written complaint with the attorney general within 180 days and bring a county circuit court civil action for damages, discretionary punitive damages, equitable relief, and prevailing-party attorney fees (for a prevailing respondent only if the case is without foundation).

headings.title: Attorney general review and discretionary legal action on complaints
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the attorney general to review each subsection 2 complaint and grants permissive authority ("may initiate") to bring legal action if deemed appropriate.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsections 1 and 3 and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1402) and verified all fingerprints. Verified parallel public-school and public-library filtering or January 1, 2003 community-standards policy duties, DESE and secretary of state rulemaking subject to chapter 536/section 536.028 and post-August 28, 2002 nonseverability clauses, section 162.091 penalty scope limited to public school personnel, and criminal/civil immunity for compliant schools, libraries, and ISPs. Retained all 6 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Public school duties for filtering or restricting public access computers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note (L. 2002 H.B. 1402). Requires public schools providing public access computers to use filtering software/ISP filter services limiting minors' access to material pornographic for minors, implement a community-standards restriction policy by January 1, 2003, or both.

headings.title: Education department enforcement rules and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs DESE to establish enforcement rules for subsection 1 subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause voiding the rulemaking grant and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2002, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Public library duties for filtering or restricting public access computers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Requires public libraries providing public access computers to use filtering software/ISP filter services limiting minors' access to material pornographic for minors, implement a community-standards restriction policy by January 1, 2003, or both.

headings.title: Secretary of state enforcement rules and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the secretary of state to establish enforcement rules for subsection 3 subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with a nonseverability clause voiding the rulemaking grant and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2002, if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Section 162.091 penalties for willful neglect by public school personnel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Subjects public school board members, officers, or employees (including library personnel) who willfully neglect or refuse to perform a duty under section 182.827 to penalties under section 162.091; preserves exact party scope limited to public school personnel.

headings.title: Criminal and civil immunity for compliant schools, libraries, and providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Grants criminal and civil damages immunity to compliant public schools, public libraries, their boards, officers, employees, and trustees, and compliant internet service providers if a minor accesses material pornographic for minors on a public-school or public-library public access computer.
